dengue.pdf.37: Table 2: Table showing clinical differentiation among dengue, chikungunya and zika. HIGH: Dengue—thrombocytopenia, progressive increase in hematocrit, leukopenia; Chikungunya—arthralgias; Zika—pruritus. MODERATE: Dengue—anorexia or hyporexia, vomiting, abdominal pain, chills, hemorrhages (includes bleeding on the skin, mucous membranes, or both); Chikungunya—rash, conjunctivitis, arthritis, myalgias or bone pain; Zika—rash, conjunctivitis. LOW: Dengue—retro-ocular pain, hepatomegaly, headache, diarrhea, dysgeusia, cough, elevated transaminases, positive tourniquet test; Chikungunya—hemorrhages (includes bleeding on the skin, mucous membranes, or both); Zika—adenopathies, pharyngitis or odynophagia. Anorexia or hyporexia; vomiting; abdominal pain; chills; hemorrhages (includes bleeding on the skin, mucous membranes, or both).
